insights.title: Advertising lifts visits, and there is no real doubt about the direction
insights.detail: Visit rate rose from 3.82% to 4.85% (95% CI +1.005 pp to +1.063 pp). Posterior probability that treatment is better: > 99.99%.

insights.title: The raw comparison overstates the effect
insights.detail: The arms are not perfectly comparable (a model tells them apart with AUC 0.510). Adjusting for the 12 features gives +0.745 pp, 28% below the raw +1.034 pp. Plan on the adjusted number.

insights.title: The top 10% of users deliver 83% of all incremental visits
insights.detail: Ranked by the S-learner (gradient boosting) model on held-out users, the top 10% gain +6.07 pp each versus +0.73 pp on average: 8× the typical response.

insights.title: Blanket advertising loses money; targeting makes it profitable
insights.detail: Illustrative assumptions (cost 0.05 per user, value 5 per visit, 1M users): treating everyone returns -13,272, treating the top 14% returns 25,582 (95% interval 23,234 to 27,708). Coverage chosen on validation, profit measured on test.

insights.title: Ranking by likely response gets most of the way; uplift modelling adds a little
insights.detail: The best uplift model beats a plain response model by 8% on gain over random for visits (paired 95% CI excludes zero). For conversions, T-learner (gradient boosting), S-learner (gradient boosting) are significantly worse than the response baseline. Conversion gain over random for the response baseline: 0.43 per 1,000 users.

insights.title: The model's predicted differences match what the data shows
insights.detail: Across 45 feature segments, mean predicted uplift tracks the observed doubly-robust uplift (correlation 0.99, average gap 0.043 pp). Shuffling f0 costs the most ranking value (10% of the gain).

insights.title: Persuadables all sit off f8's typical value
insights.detail: 100% of the top 10% by predicted uplift have a non-modal f8, against 42% of everyone else (standardised difference -2.06). Features are anonymised, so this is a targeting signal, not an explanation.

insights.title: The effect is far above what this test could detect
insights.detail: With 13,979,592 users at 85%/15% the minimum detectable effect is +0.040 pp; the observed effect is 26 times larger. Detecting a 5% relative lift would need about 638,939 users (4.6% of this sample).

insights.title: Checking results 10 times would push false positives from 5% to 19%
insights.detail: Simulation: stopping at the first p < 0.05 across 10 looks gives a 19% false-positive rate instead of 5%. An O'Brien-Fleming boundary restores 5.2% and still stops early, using 76% of the planned sample on average when the effect is real.

insights.title: A 'quick sample' of this file would have no control group
insights.detail: 12 of 20 position blocks contain only one arm, and at least the first 4,892,860 rows are all treated. Every split and sample here uses a salted hash of row position instead.

concentration.note: 100% = incremental outcomes from treating everyone. Values above 100% mean the remaining users are, on net, hurt or unmoved.

prior.description: Beta(1, 1) on each arm's rate (uniform when 1, 1)
